nodes.text: Is it true that, almost surely, a random graph on $n$ vertices with $\geq (\tfrac{1}{2}+\epsilon)n\log n$ edges is Hamiltonian?

#746 : [Er71,p.98] [Er81,p.16] [Er82e,p.69] graph theory A conjecture of Erdős and Rényi [ErRe66] , who proved that almost surely such a graph has a perfect matching (when $n$ is even). This is true. Pósa [Po76] proved that almost surely a random graph with $\geq Cn\log n$ edges is Hamiltonian for some large constant $C$, and Korshunov [Ko77] proved that\[\geq \frac{1}{2}n\log n+\frac{1}{2}n\log\log n+w(n)n\]edges suffices, for any function $w$ which $\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Komlós and Szemerédi [KoSz83] proved the stronger result that with\[\frac{1}{2}n\log n+\frac{1}{2}n\log\log n+cn\]edges the probability that the graph is Hamiltonian tends to $e^{-e^{-2c}}$ as $n\to \infty$.
